answer: I built a 6-spin chain (J=1, h=1, all spins up, time 1) as 4 Trotter steps of ZZ and X rotations. I made stretched copies at 3x and 5x noise by gate folding (U, then U followed by U-dagger and U again, repeated). I submitted all 3 circuits as one job to garnet:mock (job 01a16062-7183-7476-9beb-e381043e4bdd, 1000 shots each). The mock only checks the job compiles and returns random bits, so its counts are not used. I got the real noisy numbers from IQMFakeGarnet, the local noisy simulator (20000 shots each). Average magnetization came out at 0.1194 (1x), 0.0652 (3x) and 0.0473 (5x). More noise drags the value toward 0, as expected. I fitted these with an exponential decay and extrapolated back to zero noise. That gave 0.1517 (a straight-line fit gives 0.1314). The exact answer is 0.2044. The perfect Trotterized circuit gives 0.1869, which is the value ZNE can reach at best, and the rest of the gap is Trotter error. The raw 1x value was 0.085 below exact, and the mitigated value is 0.053 below it, so the error shrank by roughly 38 percent. Principle: you cannot remove noise, but you can measure how the answer changes as you deliberately add more noise and extrapolate back to the no-noise point. The cost is extra circuit depth and amplified statistical error. Scripts and output are in the worktree: zne.py and out.json.
